content:
anya: Heads up — I found KMS-wrapped tokens in partner logs in GCS (don't paste secrets). Bucket: `gs://partner-ingest/logs/2026-03-20/requests.jsonl`. Looks like base64 ciphertext with KMS metadata. ping @lee @samir for triage

lee: can you paste one redacted line (no plaintext creds) so we can confirm format?

anya: here's a redacted JSON line (replaced 90% of blob with Xs):
```json
{"timestamp":"2026-03-20T14:12:03Z","request_id":"r123","user":"partner-ingest","payload":{"kms_ciphertext":"CiQAXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX","kms_key":"projects/1234/locations/global/keyRings/partners/cryptoKeys/ingest"}}
```

samir: that looks like a wrapped ciphertext (cloud KMS resource included). Two immediate questions: (1) Did partner log plaintext before wrapping? (2) Which service accounts can decrypt that key?

maria: partner-infra owns the integration, i'll DM them now. we should assume worst-case (they logged plaintext at some point). proposed immediate steps: 1) gather affected SA list, 2) rotate cryptoKey / create new key version, 3) suspend partner SA access to decrypt, 4) rotate any downstream tokens that could have been derived. also we should enable audit export for the cryptoKey and the bucket.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (P2) — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-credential-exposure — add notes and affected resources.

oncall-ops: i'm oncall — can run rotation/disable in ~30m. Need list of affected SAs and a short maintenance window. If partner can rewrap, we can coordinate; otherwise we'll force-rotate downstream credentials and revoke tokens.

anya: redacted SA I found in related log lines: `partner-ingest@partner.gserviceaccount.com`. Affected time window (~2026-03-20T13:50 - 2026-03-20T15:05). i will run a log sweep for similar patterns and attach sample IDs to the incident.

samir: rotation plan (short):
1) create new cryptoKeyVersion on `projects/1234/.../cryptoKeys/ingest`
2) disable old cryptoKeyVersion so it can't decrypt (allow rewrap only if partner proves they re-encrypted)
3) issue new tokens / creds for any downstream consumers and invalidate old ones
4) audit and export logs to BigQuery for forensic queries

If partner cannot rewrap, we MUST rotate downstream secrets. We'll also add a short TTL on any new key bindings.

maria: I'll open partner Jira and book a 1hr window at 1600 UTC for the rotation and testing. I'll also request partner confirm whether they persisted plaintext elsewhere. For audit sink: `gcloud logging sinks create kms-audit-sink ...` and export to our secure project.

lee: RBAC note: remove direct `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` from partner SA on the cryptoKey. Replace with a short-lived impersonation pattern (workload identity / token exchange) or a limited access proxy. We should also add a conditional binding if possible (time-limited).

anya: i've started tagging all matching log lines and added evidence to INC-2026-042. also capturing object metadata (generation, ACLs).

samir: post-rotation: run ingest jobs in staging with the new key version and confirm no regressions. run a scripted decrypt test using new key version only.

oncall-ops: action owners assigned: maria (partner contact + schedule), lee (IAM policy changes), samir (kms rotate/rekey + tests), anya (log sweep + evidence). I'll lead the actual key disable/enable steps during the window. ETA ~35m.

maria: :thumbsup: will ping partner and update Jira.

sec-bot: Reminder: ensure audit log retention for this incident is extended and add a timeline entry in INC-2026-042.

lee: small follow-up — add a deny policy on the bucket to prevent partner-managed logging of sensitive headers/fields (redaction agent) and add a logging policy to block public ACLs.

anya: thanks all — i'll DM partner now and attach samples to the ticket. will update here when sweep completes.
